title: Defending Our Right to Submit Evidence Against U.S. Officials to the International Criminal Court
author: Tariq Ra’ouf – Anna Marie Stenberg
content:

_Tariq Ra’ouf is a Palestinian American author, an activist with the_[ _Global
Sumud Flotilla_](https://www.globalsumudflotilla.org/) _, and a co-founder
of_[ _Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide_](https://www.taxpayeralliance.net/)
_(TAAG). Anna Marie Stenberg is a US taxpaying citizen of Lebanese descent, a
lifelong human rights advocate, and co-founder of TAAG. These are the
statements that they gave at a_[ _press
conference_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swPpN_mH0h4) _convened by the
human rights organization_[ _DAWN_](https://dawnmena.org/) _and TAAG to
announce the filing of a_[ _federal lawsuit_](https://dawnmena.org/u-s-groups-
sue-trump-admin-over-icc-sanctions-that-muzzle-palestine-advocacy/) _on July
15, 2026, against the Trump Administration for its_[ _Executive
Order_](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/02/imposing-
sanctions-on-the-international-criminal-court/) _on the International Criminal
Court (ICC). This order gives the Administration the power to sanction
“foreigners” involved in ICC investigations of U.S. and Israeli officials. The
order also prohibits U.S. citizens from providing or receiving “services” to
and from these sanctioned individuals and organizaitons. In their lawsuit,
TAAG and DAWN argue that this violates the 1st Amendment rights of U.S.
citizens to share information and evidence with the ICC against U.S.
officials, as well as to communicate and work with sanctioned individuals such
as UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese and sanctioned organizations like
the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights._

_In these two statements, Tariq and Anna Marie explain why they are among the
TAAG plaintiffs and why the lawsuit matters. TAAG and DAWN are seeking an
injunction from a federal judge to protect their right to submit evidence to
the ICC against U.S. and Israeli officials and to communicate with the above
named sanctioned parties. TAAG members have gathered massive evidence against
Trump, Rubio, and other U.S. officials for their participation in the ongoing
genocide in Palestinian that they hope to submit to the ICC._

**Tariq Ra’ouf’s Statement:**

Over the last three years, 49 of my family members have been killed by
American-made and funded weaponry, and now the United States is trying to
avoid accountability by going against the International Criminal Court and
anyone who dares to work with them.

Just this week, Marco Rubio and the United States have doubled down on their
attacks on the International Criminal Court, with Rubio writing a lengthy and
pathetic opinion piece in the _Wall Street Journal_ , explaining why the US is
choosing “to dismantle” the ICC. He claims that the court’s actions against US
officials are “illegitimate interventions” that interfere with American
military and law enforcement operations, and in a subsequent video released on
Twitter Rubio says, “If we stand idle, [the US] will be at the mercy of
foreign judges, thousands of miles away – facing the constant risk of
prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called ‘crime’ of defending their
own country.”

But here’s the thing: the word 'defense' has been used to justify some of the
most serious violations of international humanitarian law, and acts of pure
depravity quite literally, for as long as this country has existed. It began
with the idea of settlers coming to America and “defending” themselves against
people they called “savages,” as early American militias ransacked, pilfered
and decimated Native American villages in order to claim the very land the
United States is built on. Today, the idea of “self-defense” is used to excuse
the indefensible—the funding and arming of Israel's genocide in Palestine. The
United Nations Commission of Inquiry has confirmed that Israel has
deliberately and illegally targeted Palestinian children, with at least 20,179
children killed and 44,143 children injured since October 7. There is no
defending such hostile and inhumane actions. The International Criminal Court
is one of the only mechanisms the world has to hold those responsible
accountable for these crimes.

The United States wants to say that because they are not a state party to the
Rome Statute that founded the International Criminal Court, that the ICC has
no jurisdiction, but article 12(2)(a) of the Rome Statute expressly authorizes
the ICC to exercise jurisdiction over crimes committed on the territory of a
State Party—regardless of the perpetrator's nationality. Palestine is a State
Party, and any individuals who provide the weapons and support that make these
crimes possible are participating in crimes committed on Palestinian
territory. Therefore, the ICC has every right to hold the US and Israeli
officials accountable for their crimes.

And as Americans, we have every right to work with international organizations
and foreign nationals who are trying to use the ICC to seek justice,
especially considering the fact that our own government has become so hostile
towards anyone that dares to fight back here at home. It makes me think about
the people who are trying to stop ICE from illegally kidnapping law-abiding
individuals, and how they are called terrorists and shot in the face; and this
kind of behavior from US officials at the international level is just another
form of the same violence. We are standing at a crossroads, trying to prevent
the US from committing more crimes, the same way activists in the US are
standing in front of ICE, and this attempt by Rubio is the US’s attempt to
shoot justice in the face, but we will not be deterred by such repugnant
hubris.

I refuse to sit by and watch this government kill my cousins, aunts and uncles
and try to worm their way out of accountability. One of my aunts was killed
when she was at a Gaza Humanitarian Fund aid distribution site — she was
trying to get flour to feed her family and she was shot down, like so many
other hungry and displaced Palestinians who came to these places seeking help
only to find more death and destruction. If we sit back and allow the United
States to try and dismantle one of the only mechanisms this world has for
seeking justice, they will continue their tradition of “defending” themselves
with more terrorism and violence.

As American taxpayers, it is our duty to stand up and fight against the way
our tax dollars are being used. No longer will we sit down as money from our
paychecks is being used to kill children, while our own children are lacking
the healthcare and education they deserve. Over the last three years, I’m
happy to say the number of Americans who have woken up to the lies of
“defense” that this nation keeps telling has skyrocketed, and I know that no
matter what happens next, there is no turning back to the days we believed
this nation has ever defended anything other than its thirst for power.

**Anna Marie Stenberg’s Statement:**

TAAG is a grassroots organization of U.S. taxpayers who are committed to
holding U.S. officials criminally accountable for their participation in and
enabling the ongoing genocide in Palestine.

Over the past 2 1/2 years, TAAG members have not stood idly by while U.S.
officials used our tax dollars to carry out crimes against humanity in
Palestine. This Genocide could not be happening without the participation of
the U.S. gov. officials using our tax dollars. TAAG members have tried
everything within the U.S. to hold these officialsaccountable—through
legislative engagement, legal action, public campaigns, and direct appeals to
government officials. These efforts have been met with silence and inaction.
U.S. officials continue to operate with full impunity, and there is no genuine
domestic proceeding that could or would hold them accountable for these
international crimes. This must be stopped!

We now turn to the ICC as the only international body that can investigate,
arrest, and prosecute government officials for genocide and other crimes
against humanity.

For months, members of TAAG have gathered substantial evidence of the
participation of U.S. officials, most notably Trump and Rubio in the crime of
genocide. For instance, the US has continued to supply Israel with 2000-pound
bombs made by General Dynamics here in America that are being used to level
Gaza and kill untold numbers of children, men, women, mothers, and fathers.

Another example of the crime of genocide is that while Israel blocked all
food, medicines and humanitarian assistance from entering Gaza, the U.S.
defunded UNRWA, which had 400 food distribution sites in Gaza and the US
supported the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation GHF that had only 4 distribution
sites for all of Gaza during a starvation epidemic. By the end of May, 2025 it
had been well documented that at least 400 Palestinians seeking food had been
shot and killed at or near these GHF sites. Despite this, Secretary of State
Marco Rubio authorized $30 million in U.S. taxpayer funds to be sent to the
GHF. The killings continued! By September 17, 2025, the United Nations had
recorded a total of at least 2,319 people killed their only crime was trying
to obtain food and humanitarian assistance.

TAAG is prepared to submit that evidence and much more to the ICC Office of
the Prosecutor. We are blocked in doing so by Trump’s executive order and that
is why we are proud to be co-plaintiffs with DAWN and stand together today in
filing this lawsuit.

Personally, as a mother and a grandmother, this is something I must do! I
cannot, I will not!, be a bystander to Genocide! We welcome others joining us
in this effort to ensure that all Americans obey the law and do not commit
genocide, crimes against humanity, or war crimes.
